findings.issue: 結納品 is read ゆいのうひん, never けつのうひん (結納 'betrothal gifts' has the irregular reading ゆいのう). The kana teaches a nonexistent reading of the key word.
findings.current: えっ、けつのうひんになんじゅうまんえん?
findings.suggested: えっ、ゆいのうひんになんじゅうまんえん?

findings.issue: Encodes the same wrong reading of 結納品: ketsunouhin should be yuinouhin.
Token 結 (first component of 結納品) is read ゆい in this word, not けつ (結納 = ゆいのう). With the following token 納品=のうひん kept as is, ゆい restores the correct overall reading ゆいのうひん.
何 before を is read なに, never なん (なん occurs only before だ/の/で and counters). 何をしていた = なにをしていた.
findings.current: いままでいったいなんをしていたんだ!
findings.suggested: いままでいったいなにをしていたんだ!

findings.issue: Encodes the wrong reading nan(+o) for 何を; correct is nani o.
何 as direct object followed by を is read なに, not なん.

en reads に as additive ('plus'), but lit_en ('on betrothal gifts (に)'), pt ('só de presentes de noivado') and both expl fields treat に as the expenditure target ('for'). Internally contradictory; the expenditure reading is the natural one — align en with the rest.
findings.current: Eh? Hundreds of thousands of Yen plus betrothal gifts?
findings.suggested: Eh? Hundreds of thousands of yen for the betrothal gifts?

findings.issue: pt (and expl/token gloss) render かかれ as 'attack' ('Ataquem!'), but the paired human en is 'Start, dammit!' (かかる = start/get going, e.g. an engine or task) — a direct sense contradiction visible to learners. Align pt with the attested en (and re-sense expl_en/expl_pt and the かかれ gloss), or re-verify the Tatoeba context.
にも ('also to the pool') is dropped from the natural en, while pt keeps 'também' and lit_en keeps 'also' — en loses the nuance and is inconsistent with the other fields.
findings.current: That was when I started going to the pool for exercise.
findings.suggested: That was when I also started going to the pool for exercise.
